To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prlA andprlG suppressors of signal sequence defects function by the same mechanism and that this mechanism is a reduction in the requirement for signal recognition.
prlA and some prlG alleles are suppressors of the requirement for a signal sequence in the export of LamB.
PrlA and PrlG suppressors of defective signal sequences function in the export pathway to suppress the requirement for signal recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of prlA and, to a lesser extent, prlG suppressers that act at a step in protein export that normally requires a functional signal sequence.
the role of PrlA and its suppressors in the export of proteins from the cytoplasm to the periplasm in Escherichia coil.
the role of the signal sequence in export and with the function of the prlA and the prlG gene products in the protein export pathway of E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prlA and the prlG alleles are suppressor alleles that allow the export of proteins that are normally exported with low efficiency or not at all.
prlA and, to a lesser extent, prlG suppress the requirement for signal sequences.
the prlA and the prlG mutations are suppressors of the requirement for signal peptide recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the signal sequence is required for export of the outer membrane protein LamB, but that the signal sequence can be bypassed by a suppressor mutation that reduces the requirement for signal recognition.
signal sequence recognition is a stringent requirement of the export pathway in E. coli. PrlA and PrlG suppressors reduce signal sequence requirements for protein export.
the signal sequence of LamB is required for efficient export, and this signal sequence requirement can be overcome in the absence of a proofreading activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PrlA and PflG have a dual function in the export pathway: they are required for the export of proteins with defective signal sequences and also for the export of signal sequences that lack a signal peptide.
the export pathway is extremely sensitive to the structure of the signal sequence and that the prlA andprlG genes are important in the proofreading of this structure.

the prl suppressors do not function by allowing the secretion of proteins that would normally be excluded from the export pathway, but rather by allowing the secretion to proceed with a lower fidelity.
